text: DSH DeepSeek Usage 是面向 DSH 网页端的 DeepSeek 用量面板，在侧边栏提供入口并打开统计界面。它通过宿主路由查询账户余额、读取本地会话记录，并显示 Token 用量、费用估算、模型与工作区统计以及当前峰谷时段。面板还提供版本提示和配置界面，适合想在 DSH 中集中查看 DeepSeek 余额和会话使用情况的用户。余额查询需要可选的 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY；本地统计无需密钥。

DSH DeepSeek Usage adds a panel to the DSH web sidebar. It queries account balance and aggregates local session records into token, cost, model, and workspace statistics, with current peak or off-peak periods. A DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is optional for balance lookup; local statistics need no key.

Show token usage grouped by model and workspace from my local sessions.

DSH DeepSeek Usage 的功能「账户余额」：面板向 DeepSeek 余额接口查询账户总额、充值和赠送余额；从侧栏打开用量面板即可查看。余额请求使用宿主凭据。
DSH DeepSeek Usage 的功能「本地用量分析」：插件读取持久化会话记录并汇总 Token 与费用，支持按时间、模型和工作区查看；面板同时显示图表和活动热力图。
DSH DeepSeek Usage 的功能「峰谷时段和价格估算」：插件按模型价格及北京时间峰谷、周末和节假日日历估算官方 DeepSeek 调用费用，并在面板显示当前时段信息。
DSH DeepSeek Usage 使用 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY 向 api.deepseek.com 查询账户余额；不配置密钥时，本地会话用量统计仍可使用。见 lib/index.js:1044-1059。

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · dsh-deepseek-usage：> Note: DeepSeek's API does not expose an account-level usage endpoint (all candidate paths return 404 in practice). The usage data therefore comes from your local session logs — which contain the exact `usage` values returned by the official API for every request.

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Install (pick one)：You need **Node.js** first (download from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org)).

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Option A: Install straight from GitHub (recommended, one command)：Paste this into a terminal:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage.git#v0.7.1
```

**Don't have `dsh` installed globally?** Use this instead (`npx` downloads it on first run):

```sh
npx --yes @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage.git#v0.7.1
```

> Tip: if the installer complains that `pnpm` is missing, run `npm install -g pnpm` and retry.

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Optional: configure an API key (for the balance card)：Add a line to `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` (replace `sk-xxxx` with your key):

```yaml
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY: sk-xxxx
```

Or set the `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` environment variable. Without a key, local usage statistics still work; the balance card just shows a hint.

text:
@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Uninstall：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove @xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage
```

Then restart `dsh web` and refresh the page.

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Privacy：The plugin **never embeds an API key** (no key material in the package). The key is resolved at runtime from the *recipient's own* machine — `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` or the environment — and only on the host (server) side; the browser bundle never sees it. Safe to share.

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Layout：```
lib/index.js       host half — /dsh-usage/balance + /dsh-usage/local + /dsh-usage/period routes
lib/client.js      browser half — sidebar action + panel (hand-built bundle, no build step)
cordis.patch.yml   the plugin's own patch layer (dsh.bundle — auto-activated on install)
install.sh         one-shot installer

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Configuration (optional, usually not needed)：Override row config by id in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: deepseek-usage
  config:
    balanceTtlMs: 60000        # balance cache TTL (ms)
    maxSessions: 100           # most-recent sessions to replay

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Configuration (optional, usually not needed)：> **Holidays move every year — and you don't have to do anything.** The State
> Council publishes the next year's schedule late in the current one, so the
> plugin reads [`holidays.json`](holidays.json) from this repository (6-hour
> cache). The maintainer adding the new year to that one file is the entire
> yearly step: installed plugins pick it up on their next refresh, with no
> release and no user action. Precedence is **your `holidayRanges` → remote
> `holidays.json` → the built-in 2026 table**, so a local override or a broken
> download never leaves you without a calendar; a malformed file is discarded
> whole rather than half-applied. If the calendar does not cover the current
> year, the panel says so instead of quietly over-estimating holidays.
> Make-up working weekends need no entry — they are calendar weekends and are
> already off-peak.

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Configure it from the GUI：Everything above is also editable without touching YAML: open **sidebar → 插件 (Plugins) →
`@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage` → the `deepseek-usage` row → 配置**. The form is generated
from the plugin's own config schema, so DSH validates every value and writes it into the
same `cordis.patch.yml` row shown above — a saved field *is* an ordinary override, and
clearing a field restores the built-in default. **Restart `dsh web` after saving**: a
config-only change is written to the profile immediately but is not hot-reloaded by the
host. Fields are grouped as *performance and refresh*, *holiday calendar*, *windows and
region (advanced)* and *pricing overrides (advanced)*; the JSON fields (`pricing`,
`peakHours`, `holidayRanges`, `holidayWorkdays`) take the same structures documented
below. Per-model rate overrides only skew the local **estimate** — official billing is
unaffected.

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Updating：**npm installs:** run `dsh plugin --profile web update @xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage`
(or re-add with the new version: `... add @xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage@X.Y.Z`).

**Git installs:** you installed a pinned snapshot, so updates are **not** automatic — but you
don't need to check for them: the plugin queries the GitHub releases feed
(hours-cached) whenever you open the usage panel and shows a **「New version
available」** banner.

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Updating：Click **「Update now」** in that banner and the plugin installs the new version for
you — no terminal involved. When it finishes the panel says so; if the interface
still looks unchanged, restart the app. (The install itself is done by the
harness's plugin manager: the panel asks it to install this package at the new
tag, and nothing else.)

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Updating：Two cases keep the copyable command instead of the button: a DSH build without
that plugin manager, and a `link:` development checkout (where re-installing
would replace your working tree with a tagged copy). Either way the command is
right there in the banner:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove @xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage
dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage.git#v0.7.1
```

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Troubleshooting：**I see `dsh: warning: ... declares no dsh.bundle — installed as a plain dependency`**

You installed an older snapshot of the repository (pnpm caches git
dependencies by commit, so an install that happened before this package
declared `dsh.bundle` keeps the old version). Fix it by reinstalling from
the pinned tag:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove @xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage
dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage.git#v0.7.1
```

@xavier711/dsh-deepseek-usage README · Troubleshooting：Then restart `dsh web` and refresh the page.

**The 「用量」 entry does not appear after installing**

Make sure the web server was restarted after the install (`Ctrl+C` in the
`dsh web` terminal, then run it again) and that you hard-refresh the browser
page (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R).
